rules.title: Absence limits
rules.text: For the 5-year route: no more than 450 days outside the UK in 5 years, and 90 days in the last 12 months. For the 3-year spouse route: 270 days in 3 years and 90 in the last 12 months. Use the calculator on this page.

rules.title: Good character
rules.text: The Home Office looks at criminal records, immigration breaches, debts and honesty in past applications. Declare everything; we advise on how.

rules.title: Married to a British citizen
rules.text: You can apply as soon as you have ILR, with a 3-year residence requirement.

rules.title: The citizenship ceremony
rules.text: After approval you attend a ceremony, usually within 3 months, and become British on that day.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Who can apply for British citizenship?
sections.text: Most adults become British by naturalisation. You can usually apply if you have ILR, EU settled status or permanent residence; have lived in the UK for at least 5 years (3 if married to a British citizen); have held settled status for 12 months unless married to a British citizen; have passed the Life in the UK test; have B1 English; meet the good character requirement; and intend to keep living in the UK.

sections.heading: Registering children as British citizens
sections.text: Children born in the UK to settled parents, or whose parents became settled after their birth, may be able to register as British. We advise on the right route for your family.

faqs.q: How long after ILR can I apply for British citizenship?
faqs.a: Usually after 12 months, or straight away if you are married to a British citizen.

faqs.q: How many days can I be abroad for British citizenship?
faqs.a: No more than 450 days in the 5 years before applying, and 90 days in the last 12 months, on the standard route.

faqs.q: Do I need to give up my other nationality?
faqs.a: The UK allows dual nationality, but some countries don’t. Check your other country’s rules.
